guide.title: Steakhouses in Manhattan: Twenty-Three Rooms on the Midtown Spine
guide.intro: Thirty-two rooms on this page, and twenty-three of them stand between 34th Street and Central Park South. That is the shape of steak in Manhattan: a Midtown spine running from Royal 35 on East 35th Street up through Sparks on East 46th, Gallaghers on West 52nd and Quality Meats on West 58th, with the Grill's spit-roasted prime rib in the Seagram Building at its eastern edge. Downtown holds two — MarkJoseph at the Seaport and Wolfgang's on Greenwich Street — while Union Square, the Village and the Meatpacking District carry seven more, from Buenos Aires on East 6th Street to STK on Little West 12th. Five of the borough's most-cited chophouses already have place pages on their own neighborhood guides; this page names them and links out rather than repeating them. The Bronx's six rooms are folded in at the end.

sections.heading: Midtown: 34th Street to Central Park South
sections.body:
Twenty-three of the thirty-two rooms below sit in the twenty-four blocks between 34th Street and Central Park South, which is why this page opens here rather than downtown.

The East Side runs on Grand Central. Sparks has been on East 46th Street between Second and Third for three generations of the Cetta family. Benjamin Steakhouse is on East 41st beside the terminal and Benjamin Prime a block south on East 40th; Ben & Jack's is on East 44th; Bobby Van's takes the base of the Helmsley Building at 230 Park Avenue; The Capital Grille is in the Chrysler Center on East 42nd; and Morton's is on Fifth Avenue at 45th. Further north, Smith & Wollensky holds its green-and-white corner at Third Avenue and 49th, The Grill spit-roasts prime rib in the Seagram Building on East 52nd, and Club A runs on East 58th. Royal 35 anchors the southern end at Fifth Avenue and 35th.

The West Side is theatre district and Sixth Avenue. Gallaghers dry-ages beef in a glass locker on the West 52nd Street sidewalk. Del Frisco's Double Eagle takes three floors of 1221 Avenue of the Americas; Mastro's is in the UBS Building at 1285; Cuerno grills over charcoal at 1271. Wolfgang's Times Square room is on West 41st, Empire on West 54th, Nusr-Et on West 53rd, Hunt & Fish Club on West 44th, Brooklyn Chop House on West 47th and Churrascaria Plataforma on West 49th. Quality Meats sits on West 58th and Bourbon Steak faces the park from Central Park South.

Keens is on this stretch too, at 72 West 36th Street, and Wolfgang's original room is at 4 Park Avenue. Both are published on their own neighborhood guides and linked below.

sections.heading: Downtown: the Seaport and Tribeca
sections.body:
Two rooms, and they sit either side of the island's foot. MarkJoseph is on Water Street in the low brick blocks below the Brooklyn Bridge, built on a Prime dry-aged porterhouse served for two, three or four. Wolfgang's Tribeca room is at Greenwich and Beach Streets, a converted warehouse with a long bar and the same cut on the menu.

The Financial District's other steak room is Delmonico's at 56 Beaver Street, which reopened in 2023 and is published on the Financial District guide rather than here.

sections.heading: Union Square, the Village and the Meatpacking District
sections.body:
Seven rooms below 23rd Street, and no two of them are the same kind of steakhouse.

Hawksmoor took the restored Assembly Hall of the United Charities Building on East 22nd Street and cooks dry-aged, pasture-reared beef over live charcoal, cut by weight. Boucherie Union Square runs a dry-aged program behind a French brasserie menu at 225 Park Avenue South. Strip House has held East 12th Street since 2000, per its own account, red-walled and hung with black-and-white photographs. Golden Steer brought the Las Vegas format east in January 2026, into the One Fifth Avenue building. 4 Charles Prime Rib is a small basement room on Charles Street where prime rib is the house dish. Buenos Aires is an Argentine parrilla on East 6th Street. STK holds Little West 12th Street with a second dining room on the roof.

Two more rooms in this stretch belong to other guides: COTE, the Korean beef room at 16 West 22nd Street, and Old Homestead at 56 Ninth Avenue. Both are linked below.

sections.heading: The Bronx, folded into this page
sections.body:
The Bronx has six verified steak rooms against a bar of eight, so it gets a paragraph here instead of a page of its own. It fails on count rather than on shape: three of the six are a real cluster in Riverdale — Jake's Steakhouse on Broadway, Arnauld's Steak & Seafood and Riverdale Steak House — and they are published on the Riverdale guide. Fiorentina on East Tremont Avenue in Throgs Neck cuts USDA Prime dry-aged beef and belongs to the Throgs Neck guide. Willie's Steak House on Westchester Avenue in Parkchester and Parrilla Latina complete the six.

NYY Steak, Lobel's and the Audi Yankees Club are not counted. All three sit behind a stadium gate on game days, and a room only counts here if a reader can walk in and dine on its own terms.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's center of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. A restaurant that merely serves a good steak is out. That is why Churrascaria Plataforma and Buenos Aires are here while Minetta Tavern, with its famous burger and a good steak, is not, and neither is Balthazar: steak frites on a French menu is not a center of gravity.

faq.question: Why are Keens, Delmonico's, Old Homestead, Wolfgang's on Park Avenue and COTE named here but not listed as rooms?
faq.answer: Because they already have place pages elsewhere in this site, on the neighborhood guides for the Garment District, the Financial District, the Meatpacking District, Murray Hill and the Flatiron District. A room is published once. This page names all five and links to the guides that carry them, so nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated.

faq.question: Why does a Manhattan page carry the Bronx?
faq.answer: The Bronx measured six verified rooms against a bar of eight. It has a nameable cluster — Jake's, Arnauld's and Riverdale Steak House are all in Riverdale — so it fails on count, not on shape, and folding it into a note here was judged better than either a thin page or silence. The Riverdale three and Fiorentina in Throgs Neck are linked to their own neighborhood guides.

faq.question: Are the national chain steakhouses included?
faq.answer: The fine-dining ones are: The Capital Grille, Morton's, Smith & Wollensky, Del Frisco's, Mastro's and Bourbon Steak all have Manhattan outposts and all are on this page, each written about the room at its own address. The casual national chains — Outback, LongHorn, Texas Roadhouse — are not, because they are not destination rooms.

faq.question: Is COTE a Korean barbecue room or a steakhouse?
faq.answer: Both, which is why it appears on two food verticals. COTE at 16 West 22nd Street is a Korean beef room, a genre this collection admits, and it is also a tabletop grill room the Korean BBQ collection covers. The place page lives on the Flatiron District guide; the Korean BBQ guide for Manhattan is linked below as well.

faq.question: Which rooms did this page check and leave out?
faq.answer: Uncle Jack's on West 56th Street and Tuscany Steakhouse on West 58th have both closed, and Angus Club on East 55th could not be verified as trading. The Palm at 837 Second Avenue and Palm Too at 840 Second are permanently closed. Rooms whose current status cannot be confirmed are left off rather than published with a hedge.

photos.title: West 36th Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues, Manhattan
photos.description: A low block of West 36th Street in late afternoon sun, with a row of state flags projecting on poles above a pale two-storey frontage and a brown awning lettered Keens Steakhouse over a dark wooden door. A tattoo parlour with red awnings and neon signs adjoins it on the right, cars are parked at the kerb and two pedestrians walk along the sidewalk.
photos.author: ajay_suresh

places.name: Gallaghers Steakhouse
places.summary: Gallaghers is on West 52nd Street between Broadway and Eighth Avenue, a block from the theatres. Its dry-aging locker is glass-walled and fronts the sidewalk, so the beef hangs in view of the street, and the steaks are broiled over hickory coals.

places.name: Sparks Steak House
places.summary: Sparks is a Midtown East steakhouse on 46th Street between Second and Third Avenues, a five-minute walk from Grand Central. The sirloin is the room's signature cut and the wine list runs to hundreds of bottles.
places.history: Opened by the brothers Pasquale and Michael Cetta in the 1960s and still run by the family, per the restaurant's own account.

places.name: Smith & Wollensky
places.summary: The green-and-white corner building at Third Avenue and 49th Street is the original Smith & Wollensky. Beef is butchered and dry-aged on the premises; the steakhouse takes the main floors and Wollensky's Grill next door keeps later hours.

places.name: Benjamin Steakhouse
places.summary: Benjamin Steakhouse occupies a high, vaulted former hotel dining room on East 41st Street beside Grand Central, with a large stone fireplace at one end. The dry-aged porterhouse is carved at the table.

places.name: Benjamin Prime
places.summary: Benjamin Prime is the same family's second Midtown room, one block south on East 40th Street. It runs the same dry-aged porterhouse program in a narrower, brighter dining room.

places.name: Quality Meats
places.summary: Quality Meats is on West 58th Street a block below Central Park, fitted out like a butcher's shop with steel rails, worn wood and white tile. The menu runs to a double ribeye and a corned-beef-rubbed cut alongside the standard chops.

places.name: Club A Steakhouse
places.summary: Club A is a family-run room on East 58th Street serving USDA Prime dry-aged steaks under chandeliers and dark panelling. Live jazz plays at the front of the house on Friday and Saturday evenings.

places.name: Royal 35 Steakhouse
places.summary: Royal 35 holds the corner of East 35th Street and Fifth Avenue, a few blocks from the Empire State Building. It serves USDA Prime dry-aged steaks from a street-level dining room behind a long marble bar.

places.name: Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse
places.address: 1221 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10020
places.summary: Del Frisco's Double Eagle runs over three floors of 1221 Avenue of the Americas, with tall windows onto Sixth Avenue opposite Radio City. The beef program covers Prime steaks alongside Japanese A5 wagyu and certified Kobe.
places.history: A widely repeated claim that this room closed in 2020 is wrong; it takes reservations and serves steak on Sixth Avenue.

places.name: The Capital Grille
places.summary: The Capital Grille's Grand Central room is in the Chrysler Center on East 42nd Street. Steaks are dry-aged on site and the dining room is panelled in dark wood and hung with oil paintings.

places.name: Morton's The Steakhouse
places.summary: Morton's Manhattan room sits at 551 Fifth Avenue on the 45th Street corner, a short walk from Grand Central. It serves USDA Prime aged steaks and the chain's tableside presentation of the cuts.

places.name: Wolfgang's Steakhouse
places.summary: Wolfgang's Times Square room is on West 41st Street between Seventh and Eighth Avenues. Like the rest of the group it builds its menu on a dry-aged porterhouse carved for two, three or four.

places.name: Empire Steak House
places.summary: Empire's West 54th Street room was opened by former Peter Luger waiters and follows that template closely: USDA Prime dry-aged porterhouse carved at the table, creamed spinach and thick-cut bacon beside it.

places.name: Bobby Van's Steakhouse
places.summary: Bobby Van's Park Avenue room takes the base of the Helmsley Building beside Grand Central. Aged Prime beef and seafood are served in a marble-columned dining room looking up Park Avenue.

places.name: Hunt & Fish Club
places.summary: Hunt & Fish Club is a bi-level, 180-seat steakhouse on West 44th Street in the Theater District, in nine thousand square feet of dark wood and brass. Classic cuts of beef anchor the menu, with seafood towers beside them.

places.name: Cuerno
places.address: 1271 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10020
places.summary: Cuerno is a Mexican steakhouse at 1271 Avenue of the Americas, beside Rockefeller Center. USDA Prime steaks are cooked over charcoal in a Josper oven and carried out with tortillas pressed in the kitchen.

places.name: The Grill
places.summary: The Grill occupies the landmarked Seagram Building dining room on East 52nd Street, a mid-century chophouse in travertine and bronze. Prime rib is spit-roasted and carved from a silver trolley wheeled to the table.

places.name: Churrascaria Plataforma
places.summary: Plataforma is a churrascaria on West 49th Street in Hell's Kitchen. The rodizio service carries skewers of picanha, sirloin and lamb through a large room, and the beef is carved straight onto the plate.
places.history: The group's Tribeca site closed in 2014; the West 49th Street room is the one that remained.

places.name: Ben & Jack's Steakhouse
places.summary: Ben & Jack's is on East 44th Street between Second and Third Avenues, in the base of the EVEN Hotel. The 190-seat room is built on a USDA Prime dry-aged porterhouse.
places.history: The restaurant returned to this address after five years away while the building was renovated, per its own account of the move.

places.name: Nusr-Et Steakhouse
places.summary: Nusr-Et's New York room is on West 53rd Street just off Fifth Avenue. It is the Turkish group's steakhouse format, in which cuts are trimmed and salted in front of the dining room before they reach the grill.

places.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
places.address: 1285 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10019
places.summary: Mastro's New York room is in the UBS Building on Sixth Avenue at 51st Street. The menu lists sixteen steaks and chops, from an eight-ounce filet to a double-cut porterhouse, and a band plays at the bar most nights.

places.name: Bourbon Steak
places.address: 160 Central Park S, New York, NY 10019
places.summary: Bourbon Steak is Michael Mina's steakhouse in the JW Marriott Essex House on Central Park South, at the top of the Midtown spine. The beef is finished in butter and the dining room looks straight onto the park.

places.name: Brooklyn Chop House Times Square
places.summary: The name is Brooklyn but the room is on West 47th Street in the Theater District. Dry-aged porterhouse, New York strip and bone-in ribeye share a menu with dumplings stuffed with pastrami and cheesesteak.

places.name: MarkJoseph Steakhouse
places.summary: MarkJoseph is on Water Street in the low brick blocks below the Brooklyn Bridge. The room is built on a USDA Prime dry-aged porterhouse ordered for two, three or four.

places.name: Wolfgang's Steakhouse
places.summary: Wolfgang's Tribeca room stands at Greenwich and Beach Streets in a converted warehouse with brick walls and a long bar. The dry-aged porterhouse is the same cut the group serves uptown.

places.name: Boucherie Union Square
places.address: 225 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10003
places.summary: Boucherie's Union Square room seats 222 behind a thirty-two-foot pewter bar, under Belle Epoque posters and wooden-framed mirrors. The kitchen runs a dry-aged beef program, with the larger cuts and steak frites on the same French menu.

places.name: Buenos Aires
places.summary: Buenos Aires is an Argentine parrilla on East 6th Street, a narrow room with a temperature-controlled patio behind it. Skirt steak with chimichurri and grilled short ribs carry the menu, alongside more than a hundred Argentine wines.

places.name: Golden Steer
places.summary: The Las Vegas steakhouse opened its first room outside Nevada in January 2026, in the One Fifth Avenue building at the northern edge of Greenwich Village. Prime cuts and tableside carving carry the format east.

places.name: 4 Charles Prime Rib
places.summary: 4 Charles Prime Rib is a small, dark room below street level on Charles Street in the West Village, opened in 2016. A rib of beef roasted whole and carved to order is the house dish, and the room seats few enough that reservations go quickly.

places.name: Strip House
places.summary: Strip House is on East 12th Street off Fifth Avenue, a red-walled room hung with black-and-white photographs. The menu is built on Prime cuts, with the strip steak the room takes its name from at the center of it.

places.name: Hawksmoor NYC
places.summary: The London group's only New York room occupies the restored Assembly Hall of the landmarked United Charities Building on East 22nd Street. Dry-aged, pasture-reared beef is cooked over live charcoal and sold by weight.

places.name: STK Steakhouse
places.address: 26 Little W 12th St, New York, NY 10014
places.summary: STK's downtown room is on Little West 12th Street in the Meatpacking District, with a second bar and dining room on the fourth-floor roof. It is a steakhouse run as a night-out room, with a DJ and the cuts offered in three sizes.

entries.name: Gallaghers Steakhouse
entries.note: West 52nd Street, a block from the theatres. The aging locker is the storefront: walk past and the beef is hanging behind glass at eye level.

entries.name: Sparks Steak House
entries.note: East 46th Street between Second and Third, five minutes from Grand Central. Order the sirloin; the wine list is the other reason people come.

entries.name: Smith & Wollensky
entries.note: Third Avenue at 49th Street. This is the original of the six-city group, and the butchering and dry-aging happen upstairs from the dining room.

entries.name: Benjamin Steakhouse
entries.note: East 41st Street beside Grand Central. The vaulted ceiling and the stone fireplace are inherited from the hotel dining room that stood here.

entries.name: Benjamin Prime
entries.note: East 40th Street, one block south of the first Benjamin. Same porterhouse, narrower room, easier table on short notice.

entries.name: Quality Meats
entries.note: West 58th Street below Central Park. The butcher-shop fit-out is the point: steel rails, hooks and tile, with a double ribeye on the menu.

entries.name: Club A Steakhouse
entries.note: East 58th Street. The Selimaj family works the room, and there is live jazz at the front on Friday and Saturday nights.

entries.name: Royal 35 Steakhouse
entries.note: Fifth Avenue at East 35th Street, the southern end of the Midtown spine and the closest steakhouse to the Empire State Building.

entries.name: Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse
entries.note: Three floors at 1221 Sixth Avenue, opposite Radio City. The upper floors are where the windows are, and where the wagyu is.

entries.name: The Capital Grille
entries.note: East 42nd Street in the Chrysler Center. The chain's Grand Central outpost, dry-aging on site rather than shipping in.

entries.name: Morton's The Steakhouse
entries.note: 551 Fifth Avenue on the 45th Street corner. Morton's Manhattan room, a few minutes' walk west of Grand Central.

entries.name: Wolfgang's Steakhouse, Times Square
entries.note: West 41st Street between Seventh and Eighth. One of the group's three Manhattan rooms; the original on Park Avenue sits on the Murray Hill guide.

entries.name: Empire Steak House
entries.note: West 54th Street. Founded by Peter Luger alumni, and the porterhouse-and-creamed-spinach order reads exactly that way.

entries.name: Bobby Van's Steakhouse
entries.note: The ground floor of the Helmsley Building at 230 Park Avenue, so the view from the table is straight up the avenue.

entries.name: Hunt & Fish Club
entries.note: West 44th Street, two floors and 180 seats in the Theater District. Beef and shellfish in equal measure.

entries.name: Cuerno
entries.note: 1271 Sixth Avenue by Rockefeller Center. A Mexican steakhouse: the Prime cuts go into a Josper and come out with fresh tortillas.

entries.name: The Grill
entries.note: East 52nd Street, inside the Seagram Building's landmarked dining room. The prime rib trolley is the thing to watch for.

entries.name: Churrascaria Plataforma
entries.note: West 49th Street in Hell's Kitchen. A rodizio room: the skewers keep coming until the card on the table is turned over.

entries.name: Ben & Jack's Steakhouse
entries.note: East 44th Street, in the base of the EVEN Hotel. Back at its original address after the building was rebuilt around it.

entries.name: Nusr-Et Steakhouse
entries.note: West 53rd Street off Fifth. The trimming and salting happen in the dining room, which is half of what people book for.

entries.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
entries.note: Sixth Avenue at 51st, in the UBS Building. Sixteen cuts on the menu and live music at the bar most nights of the week.

entries.name: Bourbon Steak
entries.note: Central Park South, inside the JW Marriott Essex House. The northernmost room on this page, and the one that faces the park.

entries.name: Brooklyn Chop House Times Square
entries.note: West 47th Street, despite the name. Dry-aged porterhouse on one half of the menu, pastrami dumplings on the other.

entries.name: MarkJoseph Steakhouse
entries.note: Water Street under the Brooklyn Bridge, in the Seaport. One of only two steak rooms this page publishes below Canal Street.

entries.name: Wolfgang's Steakhouse, Tribeca
entries.note: Greenwich and Beach Streets, in a warehouse conversion with brick walls and a bar that runs most of its length.

entries.name: Boucherie Union Square
entries.note: 225 Park Avenue South. A French room with a dry-aging program behind it, which is what puts it on a steakhouse page.

entries.name: Buenos Aires
entries.note: East 6th Street in the East Village. The one Argentine parrilla on the Manhattan page; the borough's other belt of them is in Queens.

entries.name: Golden Steer
entries.note: One Fifth Avenue. The newest room here, open since January 2026, according to the operator's own announcement of the New York opening.

entries.name: 4 Charles Prime Rib
entries.note: Charles Street in the West Village, down a short stair. Small enough that the prime rib sells out and the table does not come easily.

entries.name: Strip House
entries.note: East 12th Street off Fifth. Red walls, black-and-white photographs, and the strip steak the room is named after.

entries.name: Hawksmoor NYC
entries.note: East 22nd Street, in the United Charities Building's Assembly Hall. The London group's only American room outside Chicago and Boston.

entries.name: STK Steakhouse
entries.note: Little West 12th Street, with a rooftop room above the ground-floor one. The Meatpacking District's remaining steakhouse now that Old Homestead is covered elsewhere.

links.note: Keens, at 72 West 36th Street, is a Garment District place. Its mutton chop and porterhouse sit on that guide rather than being repeated here.
Delmonico's at 56 Beaver Street, which reopened in 2023, is published on the Financial District guide.
Old Homestead at 56 Ninth Avenue is a Meatpacking District place and is carried on that guide.
Wolfgang's original room at 4 Park Avenue belongs to Murray Hill. The Times Square and Tribeca rooms are on this page.
COTE at 16 West 22nd Street, the Korean beef room, is published on the Flatiron District guide.
COTE is the one room that qualifies on both verticals: a Korean-style beef room by this collection's rule and a tabletop grill room by that one. It appears on both pages and is published on neither.
Jake's Steakhouse, Arnauld's Steak & Seafood and Riverdale Steak House are the Bronx's one real cluster, all three in Riverdale.
Fiorentina Steakhouse on East Tremont Avenue cuts USDA Prime dry-aged beef and is a Throgs Neck place.
